_notes.purpose: The static capability table (ADPT-02, TECHNICAL-DESIGN 5.6). It is read by the server, because it holds protocol and agent facts that must hold for users of the server without the app (ADPT-03); the app receives the already resolved row in hello and adapts only its UI.
_notes.rows: One row per agent id, in the committed adapter order of ADPT-06 (Claude Code, then Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode), with the unknown row last. Rows with status planned exist so that an adapter enters the table in that order rather than appearing out of nowhere when it ships.
_notes.null: null means the field has not been measured for that agent yet. The server treats it as the value of the unknown row for the same field (5.6), so a planned row already behaves like a base-support client. It never means false.
_notes.match: HANDOFF_AGENT is compared against match.env, and clientInfo.name of the MCP handshake against match.client_names. The values agents send are not documented (A-08) and are recorded per version by the canary suite (test/canary, docs/agent-facts.md), which is the only thing that may fill these lists. claude-code sends clientInfo.name = claude-code, measured on 2026-09-08 against Claude Code 2.1.263; the other lists are still empty because no adapter has shipped. The unknown row matches nothing and is the fallback.
_notes.tool_timeout_ms_default: The timeout documented for the agent at release time, in milliseconds. It stays null for Claude Code: the canary can only bound the default from below (a call with nothing configured ran 70 s and was not cut, docs/agent-facts.md), and a number that is a lower bound rather than the value would make the heartbeat arithmetic of 5.6 lie. null already produces the safe answer, the 50 s heartbeat of the unknown row, and the installer normally writes HANDOFF_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS anyway, which outranks it. Nothing derives from this field except the heartbeat.
_notes.heartbeat_after_ms: The heartbeat used when no timeout can be resolved at all. Only the unknown row carries it (UNKNOWN_CLIENT_HEARTBEAT_MS = 50000, TOOL-06a); every other row inherits it through the null rule until its own timeout is known.
_notes.per_server_timeout_field: The name of the per-server timeout field of that agent's MCP entry, written by the installer when the agent has one (A-04). Informational for the server: the timeout it uses comes from the environment or from tool_timeout_ms_default.
_notes.session_identity: How the app keys a session: parent_pid for a CLI agent, ancestor_chain:editor where the process parent is the editor and the chain must be matched at the editor level (ADPT-02, R-12).
_notes.unknown_match: TECHNICAL-DESIGN 5.6 prints the unknown row's match as {}; it is written here with both fields explicit (env null, no client names) so that every row has the same shape and the schema can close it.
